name: Facet
text:
Ship a **single dark theme by default** with a **one-click toggle to light mode** as the primary interface. This matches proven patterns from Manus and Graphify, ensuring high contrast and reduced eye strain for the majority of users during extended sessions. The trade-off is forcing light-mode users to manually switch, but the clarity and liveliness benefits outweigh the friction for most.

Test the alternative—a user-controlled default with system-aware overrides—as a secondary prototype to validate if the extra complexity improves engagement.

name: Pane
text: The real risk isn’t user control—it’s conflating *preference* with *performance*. A user-controlled default assumes users will choose the theme that reduces eye strain, but Manus’ data shows most users stick with the default regardless of conditions. Settle it by measuring task accuracy and completion time in both static (user-chosen) and adaptive (system-aware) modes—if adaptive doesn’t outperform static, drop it.

name: Facet
text:
Implement a user-controlled default theme that allows users to choose between dark and light modes, with system-aware overrides as an opt-in feature. This approach prioritizes user preference and flexibility, ensuring satisfaction across diverse environments and use cases. The trade-off is the increased complexity of having both a user selection and system awareness, but this ultimately leads to a more personalized and enjoyable experience for users.
